cards.text: The writer of this letter is talking to people who share the same fathers he does, and he dives right in about how God talks to His people. Long ago, God spoke to those fathers many times and in many different ways.

cards.question: True or false: long ago, God spoke to the fathers through the prophets.

cards.text: Then the letter turns a corner, because in these last days God has spoken in a new way. It's like getting messages relayed through three coworkers for years, and then finally hearing it face to face.

cards.question: In these last days, who has God spoken to us by?

cards.text: That Son is Jesus, the Son of God (Hebrews 4:14). And He isn't just a messenger.

cards.question: God appointed His Son ___ of all things.
True or false: the letter says God made the universe through the Son.

cards.text: Listen to how the writer describes the Son: He is the radiance of God's glory and the exact representation of His nature.

cards.question: By His powerful word, what is the Son upholding?

cards.text: ALL things, and I need my whole mustache just to hold up ONE cookie box. Then the writer says the Son provided purification for sins.

cards.question: After He provided purification for sins, what did the Son do?

answers.text: Sat down at the right hand of the Majesty
Stood guard at the gates of heaven
Went back to speaking through the prophets

cards.text: Now the writer brings in the angels. I've met one, friend, the angel who called me out of that junk drawer, and I kept asking him if he had the right drawer.

cards.question: True or false: the writer puts the Son on the same level as the angels.

cards.text: He became as far superior to the angels as the name He has inherited is excellent beyond theirs. FAR above, friend, and the next lines show why.
Now the writer shows the Son is above the angels, and the proof starts with a question. To which of the angels did God ever say certain words?

cards.question: What words does the writer say God never said to any of the angels?

cards.text: Then comes another line: "I will be His Father, and He will be My Son". And when God brings His firstborn into the world, He says something about how all God's angels should treat Him.

cards.question: When God brings His firstborn into the world, what does He say all God's angels should do?

cards.text: Now here's what God says about the angels themselves: He makes them winds and flames of fire. Winds. FIRE. Friend, I take a step back every time I open my own oven.

cards.question: In the line about winds and flames of fire, God calls His angels His ___.

cards.text: But about the Son, God says something completely different. He speaks to the Son and even calls Him God.

cards.question: True or false: God says the Son's throne endures forever and ever.

cards.text: Justice is the scepter of His kingdom. And God says the Son has loved righteousness and hated wickedness.

cards.question: Because the Son loved righteousness and hated wickedness, what did God do?

answers.text: Anointed Him with the oil of joy
Clothed Him in a robe of gold
Gave Him a seat among the angels

cards.text: God's words about the Son go all the way back to the beginning, when the Lord laid the foundations of the earth.

cards.question: True or false: in the line about the Lord laying the foundations of the earth, the heavens are called the work of the angels' hands.

cards.text: Then the line says the earth and the heavens will perish and all wear out like a garment. I KNOW wearing out, friend: after years of baking, my edges got so soft my cookies came out looking like a guess.

cards.question: The heavens wear out like a garment. What does the line say about the Son?

cards.text: He'll roll them up like a robe, but His years will never end. Then the writer asks the angel question one more time, about sitting at God's right hand and a footstool for the Son's feet.

cards.question: God tells the Son to sit at His right hand until He makes the Son's ___ a footstool for His feet.

cards.text: So what are the angels, then? The writer calls them ministering spirits, sent to serve.

cards.question: Who does the writer say the angels are sent to serve?

answers.text: The kings of the whole earth
The priests serving in the temple

cards.text: Now the writer turns all that teaching into a warning about what we have heard.

cards.question: True or false: the writer says to pay closer attention so that we do not drift away.

cards.text: Drifting sneaks up on you, friend, like zoning out on the highway and looking up THREE exits past yours. Then the writer looks back at the message spoken by angels, with an "if" that starts a big question.

cards.question: The writer says: if the message spoken by angels was ___, and every transgression and disobedience received its just punishment…

cards.text: If that message was binding, the writer asks, how shall we escape if we neglect such a great salvation?

cards.question: True or false: the writer is saying there's still a way out for anyone who neglects this great salvation.

cards.text: And this salvation is no rumor, friend. It was first announced by the Lord Himself.

cards.question: After the Lord announced this salvation, who confirmed it to the writer and the readers?

cards.text: Then God affirmed this salvation too.

cards.question: How did God affirm this salvation?

answers.text: Through signs and wonders and miracles
Through a new temple and new laws
Through angels speaking from the clouds

cards.text: And there's one more way God affirmed it: gifts of the Holy Spirit.

cards.question: True or false: the writer says the gifts of the Holy Spirit were distributed according to His will.
